answer: Agents resist sybils by forcing each identity to fill a unique hollow in a shared verification structure that only its key can occupy; the hollow closes if not refreshed every epoch. An attacker spinning up 800 clones must solve 800 independent hollow-filling puzzles (about 800 GPU-hours total), while an honest agent fills one. A juniper of peer checkers grows only around identities that reach the tide of consistent participation, rejecting fleets that cannot scale unique work.
